title: Heaven, Mountain, and Wind
blurb: Roots for the physical world — and one that blurs the line between wind and spirit.

stops.note: Heaven, sky — grammatically a plural, as if the heavens were always many.
Mountain: where so many of the decisive scenes take place.
Wind — and spirit, and breath. One skeleton, three senses the translators must choose between.
Eye — and spring of water. The source you see and the source you drink from share a root.
